main_text.p: nomine præfectus, & David Goddyn Hagesteinii Toparcha ex Nobili, in Saltu carbonario, stemmate parentibus meis notissimo oriundus. qui pietate & strenuitate cum reliquis liberis tuis præfulget. Inter quos Casparus Vosbergius primogenitus, propter dotes suas, cum in Galliis degeret, Cardinali de Richelieu non ignotus, ubi nec prætermittendus Nob. Vir Johannes Hes Dominus in Piershil & VVeena, magister equitum promptissimus ac fortissimus. Itaque vos omnes hanc vobis esse mentem oftenditis aberrare incessum ejus, qui sperat absque Deo Excelso. Tuam Veritatem quod attinet, eam clamat longa sententiarum series per multos diducta annos: quarum nullam reprehendit rerum intelligens. Denique δωροφάγος, munerum acceptores, quique pretio jus dicunt, adeo detestabaris, & etiamnunc aversaris maximè; ut te hujusmodi lucri oforem, secundum Ichthronis præceptum, agnoscant omnes, qui non laborant invidia. Sed hæc viri præstantiam arguit, nedum ut famæ detrahat. Quod in
ضَلَّ سَعْىُ مَنْ يَرْجـــا غَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى [illegible, ~6 letters]

page.notes: The Arabic line between the Latin lines is printed in Arabic script; I transcribed it as far as the scan allows, and the last words are doubtful. The Greek word δωροφάγος is uncertain in its final letters, and the scan is blurred there. Dark spots and stains at the margins are not text. The first paragraph continues from the previous page, and the Arabic line is set off in the text block, so I placed it as a foot line; its position in the original is between the lines "oftenditis" and "aberrare".
